scope: Conservative scientific evidence map for bodily self-consciousness, sleep-transition phenomena, sleep paralysis and lucid dreaming relevant to Nova Conscientia concepts. This layer provides analogues, mechanisms, clinical context and measurement precedents; it does not adjudicate metaphysical interpretations.
policy: Scientific evidence is linked to Nova concepts by explicit role, never by identity.
Experimental analogues are not assumed to be identical to spontaneous experiences.
Mechanistic findings are treated as candidate explanatory context, not automatic exhaustive explanations.
Observational associations do not become causal claims.
Small-sample and case-study findings retain their limitations.
Later studies that weaken earlier interpretations are retained rather than harmonized away.
Every study records what it does not establish.

studies.citation: Blanke O, Ortigue S, Landis T, Seeck M. Stimulating illusory own-body perceptions. Nature. 2002;419:269-270.
studies.design_summary: Repeated focal electrical stimulation of the right angular gyrus during presurgical epilepsy evaluation in one patient, with elicitation of illusory own-body perceptions, whole-body displacement sensations and an OBE-like episode.
findings: Stimulation could repeatedly alter perceived bodily location and perspective in this patient.
Somatosensory body transformations and vestibular whole-body displacement sensations were also elicited.
The authors proposed disturbed integration of somatosensory and vestibular information as a mechanism relevant to the induced OBE-like experience.

nc_links.basis: Nova Décrochage concerns a perceived shift in the center/point of perception; the case demonstrates that bodily self-location can be acutely altered by focal brain stimulation.
The stimulation elicited whole-body displacement/vestibular sensations that overlap with Nova's vestibular-proprioceptive movement phenomena.
The case provides a neurophysiological route to altered own-body perception without requiring an ontological second body.
The work is relevant to dissociations between perceived body position and self-location, although it is not a direct model of every double-localization report.

limitations: Single neurological patient with epilepsy undergoing invasive evaluation.
Stimulation-induced experience is not equivalent by default to spontaneous SHC/OBE reports.
The study cannot estimate prevalence or individual variability in the general population.
does_not_establish: That all spontaneous OBE-like experiences are caused by right angular-gyrus dysfunction.
That non-neurological interpretations are logically impossible.
That an independently existing nonphysical body is present or absent.
studies.notes: High relevance to bodily-self mechanisms; low generalizability as a case report.

studies.citation: Ehrsson HH. The experimental induction of out-of-body experiences. Science. 2007;317:1048.
studies.design_summary: Healthy participants received manipulated visual perspective together with correlated multisensory bodily information to induce an illusion of being located outside the physical body.
findings: Visual perspective combined with multisensory bodily information can shift experienced self-location.
An OBE-like illusion can be induced experimentally in healthy participants.

nc_links.basis: The experiment operationalizes a shift in experienced self-location/perspective analogous to one component of Nova Décrochage.
Participants experienced a displaced bodily perspective, relevant to alternative-body/self-location phenomenology without asserting an external body.
The paradigm demonstrates that self-location and seen-body location can be experimentally dissociated.

limitations: Laboratory illusion with controlled visual/multisensory conflict.
Not a reproduction of the full phenomenology or context of spontaneous SHC/OBE reports.
The study focuses primarily on self-location rather than transition sequences.
does_not_establish: That every SHC/OBE is a visual-multisensory illusion.
That spontaneous reports share the same initiating mechanism.
Any metaphysical conclusion about consciousness outside the body.
studies.notes: Strong experimental analogue for the self-location dimension.

studies.citation: Lenggenhager B, Tadi T, Metzinger T, Blanke O. Video ergo sum: manipulating bodily self-consciousness. Science. 2007;317:1096-1099.
studies.design_summary: Healthy participants experienced conflicting visual-somatosensory information in virtual reality while viewing a body in front of them.
findings: Participants could identify with a seen virtual body under multisensory conflict.
Participants mislocalized themselves toward the seen body outside ordinary bodily borders.
Bodily self-consciousness can be manipulated experimentally through multisensory conflict.

nc_links.basis: The experiment dissociates ordinary body position, seen-body representation and experienced self-location.
The study provides a multisensory model for experiencing an alternative body representation as self-related.
Self-location can shift toward an external body representation without requiring a literal physical displacement.

limitations: VR-induced full-body illusion rather than spontaneous altered-state transition.
Does not reproduce sleep-related or hypnagogic context.
Participants remain awake during the experimental manipulation.
does_not_establish: That spontaneous exit-like experiences are identical to VR body illusions.
That all body-double reports derive from the same multisensory mechanism.
studies.notes: Useful for decomposing self-identification, body ownership and self-location.

studies.citation: Ionta S, Heydrich L, Lenggenhager B, et al. Multisensory mechanisms in temporo-parietal cortex support self-location and first-person perspective. Neuron. 2011;70:363-374.
studies.design_summary: Robotic multisensory-conflict experiments in healthy participants combined with fMRI and lesion analysis in neurological patients with abnormal self-location.
findings: Experimentally induced self-location changes depended on visual-tactile and visual-vestibular conflict.
TPJ activity tracked changes in self-location and first-person perspective.
Lesion analysis linked abnormal self-location to TPJ damage, adding causal neurological evidence for this component.

nc_links.basis: Nova's perceived relocation/shift component can be decomposed into self-location and first-person-perspective variables that are experimentally tractable.
The work provides explicit measurable dimensions for abnormal or shifted self-location.
Altered bodily self-consciousness can arise through multisensory/TPJ mechanisms without resolving the ontology of reported alternative bodies.

limitations: The experimental manipulation isolates bodily-self components rather than recreating a complete OBE/SHC episode.
Clinical lesion findings concern neurological pathology and should not be generalized uncritically to healthy practitioners.
does_not_establish: That TPJ activity is a complete explanation of all spontaneous OBE phenomenology.
That temporal sequences such as vibration → decrochage are generated by TPJ mechanisms.
studies.notes: Strong support for treating self-location and first-person perspective as independent analytic axes.

studies.citation: Hayashi M, Katoh K, Hori T. Hypnagogic imagery and EEG activity. Percept Mot Skills. 1999;88:676-678.
studies.design_summary: Seven participants reported hypnagogic imagery content every minute while EEG during sleep onset was classified using a five-stage hypnagogic system.
findings: Reported hypnagogic imagery content changed as a function of EEG-defined hypnagogic stages.
Phenomenological change across sleep onset can be related to physiological staging rather than treated as one undifferentiated threshold.

nc_links.basis: The study shows that sleep-onset phenomenology can be paired with EEG stage rather than relying only on retrospective labels.
Hypnagogic imagery varies systematically with the electrophysiological progression of sleep onset.

limitations: Very small sample.
Brief repeated verbal reporting can itself influence the transition process.
The study addresses imagery content, not SHC/OBE transitions specifically.
does_not_establish: A unique EEG signature for every Nova hypnagogic phenomenon.
That a given subjective image reliably identifies an exact sleep stage.
studies.notes: Important precedent for coupling phenomenology to objective sleep-onset staging.

studies.citation: Sharpless BA, Barber JP. Lifetime prevalence rates of sleep paralysis: a systematic review. Sleep Med Rev. 2011;15:311-315.
studies.design_summary: Systematic review of 35 studies reporting lifetime sleep-paralysis rates, aggregating 36,533 participants.
findings: Weighted lifetime prevalence was 7.6% in the general population in the included studies.
Higher prevalence estimates were reported in student and psychiatric samples.
Sleep paralysis is sufficiently common to require explicit differentiation from rarer or more interpretively loaded phenomena.

nc_links.basis: Provides epidemiological context for a canonical NC transition phenomenon.

limitations: Substantial heterogeneity in assessment methods and sampled populations across included studies.
Prevalence estimates depend on study definitions and reporting methods.
A 2024 meta-analysis using a different study set and methods reported a substantially higher pooled prevalence, underscoring heterogeneity.
does_not_establish: That sleep paralysis explains all SHC/OBE-like episodes.
That hallucinations occurring during sleep paralysis are equivalent to all reported sensed-presence or exit phenomena.
studies.notes: Use as clinical/epidemiological context, not as a causal model of all threshold experiences.

studies.citation: Cheyne JA, Girard TA. The body unbound: vestibular-motor hallucinations and out-of-body experiences. Cortex. 2009;45:201-215.
studies.design_summary: Analysis of self-report data from two online surveys of sleep-paralysis-related vestibular-motor and OBE experiences.
findings: Vestibular-motor sensations and OBEs formed a related but structured cluster within sleep-paralysis experiences.
Vestibular and motor experiences made partly independent contributions to OBE variance.
The results were consistent with, but did not by themselves prove, a model in which anomalous vestibular-motor experiences contribute to OBE-like phenomenology during sleep paralysis.

nc_links.basis: The study maps bodily and OBE-like hallucinations specifically within sleep-paralysis episodes.
Vestibular-motor hallucinations provide a sleep-related explanatory context for floating/flying/displacement sensations.
OBE-like shifts can co-occur with anomalous vestibular-motor sensations during sleep paralysis.
Autoscopic and displaced-self experiences appear within the broader vestibular-motor/OBE cluster studied.

limitations: Online self-report survey design.
Retrospective reports and self-selection can introduce bias.
The proposed causal ordering is model-based and not experimentally manipulated.
does_not_establish: That vestibular-motor hallucinations cause all spontaneous OBEs.
That SHC reports outside sleep paralysis share the same structure.
That survey associations resolve metaphysical interpretations.
nc_links.notes: Especially relevant to keeping vestibular and motor dimensions distinct in NC.

nc_links.citation: Voss U, Holzmann R, Tuin I, Hobson JA. Lucid dreaming: a state of consciousness with features of both waking and non-lucid dreaming. Sleep. 2009;32:1191-1200.
nc_links.design_summary: Six trained volunteers underwent multi-night EEG; lucid REM episodes were signaled with predefined horizontal eye movements.
findings: Signal-verified lucid episodes occurred during REM sleep and were associated with measurable electrophysiological differences from non-lucid REM segments in this small sample.
The original paper interpreted increased frontolateral gamma activity as support for a hybrid waking/dreaming state.

nc_links.basis: Prearranged eye signals allow lucid dream events to be time-locked during verified REM sleep.
Lucidity can be operationalized behaviorally during sleep rather than inferred only after awakening.

limitations: Only six participants and a limited number of lucid episodes.
The frontolateral 40-Hz interpretation was later challenged by Baird, Tononi and LaBerge (2022), who attributed the effect to saccadic spike potential artifacts associated with higher REM density.
EEG correlates do not themselves define the phenomenological boundaries of lucidity.
does_not_establish: That lucid dreaming is physiologically a mixture of wakefulness and REM sleep.
A universal gamma-band neural signature of lucidity.
That all forms of Nova lucidity correspond to REM lucid dreaming.
nc_links.notes: Retained together with the 2022 reanalysis to preserve scientific correction rather than silently harmonize disagreement.

nc_links.citation: Baird B, Tononi G, LaBerge S. Lucid dreaming occurs in activated rapid eye movement sleep, not a mixture of sleep and wakefulness. Sleep. 2022;45:zsab294.
nc_links.design_summary: Reanalysis of 14 signal-verified lucid dreams from six participants, comparing lucid REM with baseline REM while correcting saccadic spike-potential artifacts.
findings: Lucid REM was associated with higher REM density and physiological activation within the normal range of REM variability.
After artifact correction, the previously claimed frontolateral 40-Hz difference was not supported.
The authors argued that lucid dreaming is better characterized as activated REM sleep than as a physiological mixture of waking and sleep.

nc_links.basis: Provides a more conservative physiological context for signal-verified lucid REM dreaming.
Demonstrates the importance of artifact-controlled physiological verification when assigning state-level interpretations to lucidity.

limitations: Small number of participants and lucid episodes.
Reanalysis of an existing dataset rather than a large independent replication.
Findings concern signal-verified lucid REM dreams, not every altered state involving reflective awareness.
does_not_establish: That all lucid experiences occur exclusively in REM sleep.
That subjective lucidity has one unique neural mechanism.
That absence of a 40-Hz signature invalidates the phenomenological category of lucidity.
nc_links.notes: Important corrective study for epistemic hygiene in the lucid-dreaming evidence layer.

nc_links.citation: Dresler M, Wehrle R, Spoormaker VI, et al. Neural correlates of dream lucidity obtained from contrasting lucid versus non-lucid REM sleep: a combined EEG/fMRI case study. Sleep. 2012;35:1017-1020.
nc_links.design_summary: Four experienced lucid dreamers underwent parallel EEG/fMRI night recordings; only one participant produced two verified lucid REM episodes of sufficient length for fMRI analysis.
findings: In the analyzable participant, lucid REM epochs showed increased activation in precuneus/cuneus, parietal, prefrontal and occipito-temporal regions relative to non-lucid REM.
The study provides a proof of concept for time-locking lucid phenomenology to neuroimaging.

nc_links.basis: Verified in-dream signaling can identify lucid epochs for neuroimaging comparison.
Reflective-awareness changes during dreaming can be studied with temporally anchored physiological methods.

limitations: Only one participant contributed usable fMRI lucid epochs.
Extremely limited generalizability despite sophisticated instrumentation.
Regional activation differences do not imply a unique or complete mechanism of lucidity.
does_not_establish: A general neural signature of lucid dreaming across individuals.
That the identified activations are necessary or sufficient for lucidity.
That Nova lucidity categories outside dreaming share these activations.
nc_links.notes: Methodologically valuable; inferential weight must remain low because the usable fMRI result is effectively a single-subject case.

nc_links.citation: Konkoly KR, Appel K, Chabani E, et al. Real-time dialogue between experimenters and dreamers during REM sleep. Curr Biol. 2021;31:1417-1427.e6.
nc_links.design_summary: Four independent laboratory groups tested two-way communication during polysomnographically verified REM sleep in 36 individuals using auditory/visual questions and predefined eye or facial-muscle responses.
findings: Correct answers were obtained on 29 occasions across six participants while they were in verified REM sleep and reporting lucid dreaming.
Dreamers could sometimes perceive novel questions, maintain information, perform simple computations and return volitional signals during ongoing REM dreams.
The paradigm demonstrates that selected phenomenological/cognitive variables can be queried before awakening, reducing exclusive dependence on retrospective recall.

nc_links.basis: Provides a direct precedent for real-time communication during verified lucid REM sleep.
Volitional responses during verified REM offer a stronger temporal marker of active reflective/agentive awareness than post-hoc report alone.
In-state signaling creates event markers that can be compared with later recall, useful for studying memory distortion or omission.

limitations: Successful interactive episodes occurred in a minority of participants/trials.
The paradigm requires substantial instrumentation and specialized response channels.
Results concern lucid REM dreaming and cannot simply be transferred to non-REM threshold states or SHC practice.
does_not_establish: Continuous or reliable two-way communication with every lucid dreamer.
That similar communication is feasible during Nova's full range of threshold or separation phenomena.
Any claim about extracorporeal perception.
nc_links.notes: High-value methodological precedent for future prospective NC/Phosphenic experiments.
